title: Spark Plasma Sintering and Electrospark Deposition of High Entropy Alloys with Elemental Variation

questions.broad: For high-value components operating in aggressive environments, what intervention could improve surface physical and mechanical characteristics? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should remain effective, prior evidence that would support it, and an experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.
questions.problem_constrained: For a damaged high-value component made from a material whose physical and microstructural characteristics make traditional fusion-welding repair ineffective because of hot-cracking risk, what intervention could enable continued service without replacing the entire part under aggressive operating conditions? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to traditional fusion-welding repair, the relevant operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a falsification experiment.
questions.expert_context: Traditional fusion welding can be unsuitable for repairing certain damaged high-value components because their physical and microstructural characteristics create a risk of hot cracking. For preventing or delaying surface-defect initiation, earlier work has used PVD, CVD, electroplating, and thermal diffusion to improve hardness and resistance to wear and corrosion, but these approaches can involve costly deposition equipment, pollution, or long processing times. Under the constraints of avoiding whole-part replacement and limiting these drawbacks, what intervention could repair or improve the surface for service in aggressive environments? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, the operative mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface, its processing and service boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

levels.problem_constrained: adds the material and its limitation

gap.evidence: physical and microstructural characteristics that limit the effectiveness of traditional fusion welding... especially when hot-cracking could occur
gap.reason: The introduction motivates the need for an alternative surface-repair approach that avoids hot cracking and improves component surfaces without the cost, pollution, and processing-time drawbacks of traditional treatments.
